assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Homozygous
items.clue: Having two copies of the same allele of a gene, for example TT or tt.

items.label: Deductive reasoning
items.clue: Reasoning from a general principle or theory to a conclusion about a specific case.

items.label: Genotype
items.clue: The combination of alleles that an organism has inherited, for one gene or for many.

items.label: Inductive reasoning
items.clue: Reasoning that draws a general conclusion from observations of some but not all cases.

questions.stem: What is the role of follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) in the ovarian cycle?

options.text: It causes the mature follicle to burst and release its egg at ovulation.
It stimulates the follicles to develop and to secrete oestradiol.
It is made in the corpus luteum to maintain the endometrium.
Its rise at the end of the cycle is what triggers menstruation.

questions.explanation: FSH from the pituitary stimulates a group of follicles to develop at the start of the cycle and stimulates the developing follicles to secrete oestradiol.

questions.stem: Which event occurs during fertilization in humans?

options.text: The whole sperm enters the egg, so the embryo inherits its mitochondria from both parents.
The sperm and egg nuclei fuse into a single diploid nucleus before any cell division occurs.
The sperm nucleus enters the egg but the sperm's tail and mitochondria are destroyed.
Enzymes from the sperm digest a hole in the egg membrane to let the nucleus in.

questions.explanation: After the sperm's cell membrane fuses with the egg cell membrane, the sperm nucleus enters the egg; the tail and mitochondria do not contribute to the zygote.

questions.stem: Garden pea flowers pollinate and fertilize themselves before they open. Which statement about reproduction in the pea is correct?

options.text: It is asexual, because only one parent plant takes part in the process.
Fertilization is complete as soon as the pollen has landed on the flower's stigma.
It is sexual, because meiosis makes the gametes and they fuse at fertilization.
The pollen grains, being the male gametes, fuse directly with the ovules in the ovary.

questions.stem: Which structure of an insect-pollinated flower is correctly paired with its function?

options.text: Stigma: produces pollen grains and sheds them onto the bodies of visiting insects.
Ovary: holds the seeds until the fruit ripens and the seeds are dispersed.
Petal: brightly coloured to attract insects that carry the seeds away from the plant.
Stigma: sticky surface on which pollen grains land and then germinate.

questions.explanation: The stigma is the receptive tip of the carpel; its sticky surface traps pollen brushed off a visiting insect, and the pollen tube then grows down the style.

questions.stem: Which of these is a method that promotes cross-pollination?

options.text: Transfer of pollen between different flowers on the same plant.
Male and female flowers borne on separate individual plants.
Seeds carried away from the parent plant by animals.
The stigma physically rejecting its own flower's pollen.

questions.explanation: When a species has male and female flowers on different plants, pollen must be carried from one plant to another, so every pollination is a cross-pollination.

questions.stem: In a self-incompatible plant species, pollen from a flower lands on the stigma of the same flower and germinates, but no seed is set. Which statement about self-incompatibility explains this?

options.text: It works by physically preventing the flower's own pollen from ever landing on its stigma.
It prevents inbreeding, which would otherwise cause harmful new mutations in the offspring.
It stops a plant's own pollen from fertilizing its eggs, so preventing inbreeding.
It is needed because self-fertilization would be asexual and so produce clones.

questions.stem: What is the difference between pollination and seed dispersal?

options.text: They are the same process: the wind or insect that carries the pollen also carries the seeds away.
Pollination is the fertilization of the flower; dispersal is the release of the fertilized pollen grains.
Pollination delivers pollen to the seeds already in the ovary; dispersal releases those seeds.
Pollination moves pollen to a stigma before fertilization; dispersal moves seeds after it.

questions.stem: A pea plant has the genotype Tt for the gene controlling stem height. Which statement about this plant is correct?

options.text: It has two separate genes controlling stem height, called T and t
It is heterozygous because its phenotype differs from both its parents
It is heterozygous, since it has two different alleles of one gene
It carries only the T allele in its body cells, with t only in its gametes

questions.explanation: T and t are two alleles, alternative forms of the one gene for stem height, occupying the same locus on the two homologous chromosomes. Having two different alleles is the definition of heterozygous.

questions.stem: Which list gives a human trait due to genotype only, then a trait due to environment only, then a trait due to interaction between genotype and environment, in that order?

options.text: Adult height; a facial scar; skin colour
ABO blood group; adult height; a facial scar
ABO blood group; skin colour; adult height
ABO blood group; a scar; adult height

questions.stem: A man and a woman are both unaffected carriers of the PKU allele. They already have one child with PKU. What is the probability that their next child will have PKU?
A woman with blood group A whose genotype is IAi has children with a man of blood group B whose genotype is IBi. Which blood groups are possible in their children, and with what probabilities?

options.text: Groups A, B and AB, each 1 in 3, but not group O, as neither parent is group O
Groups AB, A, B and O are all possible, each with a probability of 1 in 4
Groups A and AB only, each 1 in 2, because the IA allele is dominant to IB
Groups A and B only, each 1 in 2, since each parent passes on its own group's allele

questions.stem: In the four o'clock plant Mirabilis jalapa, a cross between a red-flowered plant and a white-flowered plant gives only pink-flowered offspring. Two of these pink plants are crossed. What phenotypes are expected in their offspring?

options.text: Pink only, because the red and white alleles have merged into a pink allele
Pink and white in a 3:1 ratio, because pink is dominant to white
Red, pink and white flowers in a 1:2:1 ratio, as both alleles persist
Flowers with red and white patches, because both alleles are expressed
